repositories.title: NetHack
repositories.review_extent: Targeted actual subsystem and purpose/notices; not whole repository, all branches, game execution or balance audit.

source_evidence.purpose_in_comparison: Base NetHack pinned source has water-damage behavior, but the sampled file contains no doortrapped or WATER_BUCKET integration.

reviewed_mechanism: README identifies NetHack 5.0 as an enhancement to the dungeon exploration game and explicitly says this pinned 5.0.1 work-in-progress is not a release (README 3-14).

Monster item use is a turn-time subsystem with intentionally stated approximations: scroll users need sight, monsters know empty-wand charges, and monsters do not generally recognize curses (muse.c 11-15).

Eligibility is body- and context-gated. Defensive use rejects no-handed monsters, prefers immediate escape and checks traps, charges, dangerous level/terrain rules, role restrictions, player teleport knowledge and healing need (muse.c 635-749). Offensive use rejects peaceful, animal, mindless, no-handed or unaligned actors; then checks remembered resistances, target position, nearby allies, chokepoints, scary terrain, and item properties (muse.c 1417-1593). Miscellaneous use is restricted by intelligence, proximity and hands, then checks current conditions and item viability (muse.c 2094-2245).

The selectors retain a concrete inventory object and action code for downstream consumers. use_defensive/use_misc then apply the effect, spend/consume the item or wand charge, move actors, and update observed knowledge as applicable (muse.c 800-915, 2382-2518). Eligibility is not equivalent to sophisticated planning: comments say selection is not prioritized and generally takes the last viable inventory item (muse.c 1446-1448, 2153-2156).

Identification is conditional on evidence, not just use. Visible wand/scroll/potion outcomes call makeknown in specific branches; ambiguous outcomes can call trycall. Player discovery state records known versus encountered and updates the inventory view (muse.c 909-912, 923-995, 1025-1034, 2432-2518; o_init.c 453-494). The player's own potion path distinguishes an unambiguous effect from an unknown/ambiguous one before makeknown or trycall (potion.c 618-641).
repositories.disposition: Independent pattern/content comparison; no engine or code dependency adopted.
notices_and_provenance: NetHack General Public License in dat/license requires preserving source notices/license and imposes same-terms/free-availability conditions on distributed derivatives; YAIR root LICENSE is MIT. Recommend an original JS implementation. No source code, source prose, labels, graphics, audio or other assets are copied or proposed. Their rights were not established by this review.

repositories.title: Tales of Maj Eyal / T-Engine4
repositories.review_extent: Targeted actual subsystem and purpose/notices; not whole repository, all branches, game execution or balance audit.
repositories.reviewed_mechanism: Talent data supplies mode/rank, resource price, cooldown, level-scaled values, use-only rules, target metadata and action/activate/deactivate callbacks. ActorTalents:useTalent checks talent cooldown before entering execution, then runs the actor preUseTalent callback before the talent action; false/nil action or failed postUseTalent stops the success path. The module Actor:preUseTalent enforces actor-level blockers (including fear/silence/form/armor), sufficient sustain reserve or available activated resource, and talent-specific on_pre_use such as requiring a two-handed weapon. On a successful activated return, Actor:postUseTalent spends the declared mana/stamina/etc and uses game energy; only after that succeeds does ActorTalents start the declared cooldown. The reviewed action consumer applies actual effects directly: Stunning Blow attacks the target and calls target:setEffect only for a landed hit the target can receive; Manathrust projects bolt or beam damage based on rank. Sustained activation records the activate() return in actor.sustain_talents after postUseTalent; deactivation calls deactivate(), reverses stored temporary/resource effects and clears the active record. The engine Savefile contract says the Game is recursively serialized with its contained objects; ActorTalents initializes talents, talents_cd and sustain_talents from actor fields, so these are actor-owned state rather than ephemeral UI. This is source evidence for the host lifecycle, not a gameplay or reload test.
repositories.disposition: Independent pattern/content comparison; no engine or code dependency adopted.

repositories.reviewed_mechanism: Possession accepts only a corpse item, only while in the soul form, and gates the target monster race level against a cap derived from the player's maximum level; it consumes that corpse on success. The active body determines attack blows/effects, available spells, selected stats and abilities, armor/speed bonuses, resistances and equipment compatibility. Leaving the body can destroy/decay it. At less than one-quarter health, each hit creates a one-in-66 ejection chance; ejection may leave a corpse one time in three, otherwise the old body decays, then resets the possessor to soul form at full health. Form changes recalculate bonuses, HP/mana and equipment, clamp/restore level against the new form's maximum, and append body history that has explicit save/load routines. Separately, ordinary monster experience calls mon_change_race when the race's next_exp threshold is reached, except chameleons; this is not possession or player-form acquisition and should remain a distinct possible world-actor progression rule.
repositories.disposition: Independent pattern/content comparison; no engine or code dependency adopted.

repositories.review_extent: Targeted actual subsystem and purpose/notices; not whole repository, all branches, game execution or balance audit.
repositories.reviewed_mechanism: This third-party wrapper over a specific bondage.js fork accepts Yarn text, optional variable storage/functions and a command handler, then yields text, options and command results (README; src/yarn-bound.js 1-43, 130-164). Its lookahead toggles runner lookahead while it advances to infer end-of-dialogue and combine text/options; its comments say command sequences can be handled during that lookahead and that one conditional edge case causes commands to be handled prematurely (src/yarn-bound.js 56-127). README says Yarn function callbacks should have no side effects because evaluation may occur unexpectedly. README also explicitly records missing/supplemental Yarn features. YarnBound therefore offers a narrow browser cursor, with behavior bounded by its wrapper and dependency, not a supported official Yarn runtime.

reference_works.title: Elin
observed_facts: The developer describes a roguelike sandbox combining crafting, survival, and base building/management.
The product page lists housing, fishing, music, farming, livestock breeding, childbirth, shops, tourism, companions, and pets among its play options.
The developer describes a mix of generated content and fixed content faithful to its setting.
reference_works.inference_and_yair_connection: Useful contrast for letting home, ordinary skills, and local services create more than one life route. Current YAIR owners include village/everyday-life activities, site projects, jobs, native stock, and world instances. The useful question is which one optional home service or profession creates a new capability or visit reason, not whether to add a settlement-management layer.
reference_works.limits_and_rights: Store-page feature claims only; no game session, mechanics tracing, save behavior, or content/assets were reviewed. Elin is a commercial game. Use this as a design comparison; do not copy its names, prose, art, code, or setting.

reference_works.title: Soulash 2

source_routes.kind: developer-published Steam announcements, including v0.10 Living World and v0.10.3 Economy

observed_facts: The product page describes simulated history, skill-based progression, customizable abilities, material-based crafting, building, and trading; it identifies the title as Early Access.

The developer's Living World announcement describes settlement events with lasting consequences, wilderness events and weather, NPC adventuring groups, and a new world-event data-file type for modders.
The developer's Economy announcement describes a skill whose use unlocks more ways to influence the city, move resources, and direct other workers.
reference_works.inference_and_yair_connection: A strong comparator for joining an ordinary skill to settlement influence, funded labor, and off-screen events. YAIR already owns skills, jobs, actors, causes, simulation effects, settlement/site facts, clocks, and publication. A small authored event can reuse these owners; Soulash's autonomous settlement scale is not a required first-milestone system.
reference_works.limits_and_rights: Official feature descriptions and announcements only, not code or a playthrough; no claim about the complete event or migration implementation. The work is commercial and Early Access. No code, wording, names, art, or world content is proposed for copying.

reference_works.title: Caves of Qud
observed_facts: The product page describes physical simulation, including digging, corrosive mutation, and melting terrain according to material melting points.

The official press kit describes actors with skills, equipment, faction allegiances, and body parts; it gives psionic domination of a spider as an example of inhabiting its body and using its capabilities.
The developer describes more than seventy factions and an authored story woven through physical, social, and historical simulation.
reference_works.inference_and_yair_connection: Compare one body/source-specific capability and one environmental interaction at a time. Current YAIR owners include body progression, capabilities and power models, native combat, people/knowledge, and world/situation facts. The connection is a useful counter or passage rule that changes because of the actual actor body or owned faculty, not importing Qud's tile simulation or faction count.
reference_works.limits_and_rights: Official descriptions only; no code, full simulation trace, or playthrough. Caves of Qud is commercial. Do not copy its lore, factions, mutation text, artwork, or code.

reference_works.title: Dwarf Fortress
observed_facts: The developer describes generated worlds with civilizations, personalities, creatures, cultures, and histories, and inhabitants with simulated personalities.
The Steam description lists cultures, taverns, libraries, temples, animal training, bookbinding, and material-specific crafting as parts of its simulation.
The product page distinguishes fortress management from an embodied Adventure mode in which a player can explore civilizations and recruit followers.
reference_works.inference_and_yair_connection: Useful contrast for giving independent lives a durable history and for connecting a local settlement to an embodied traveler. YAIR's people, attributed knowledge, situations, chronicle, native combat, and world-instance owners cover smaller authored examples; the comparator does not establish that YAIR needs procedural civilization generation.
reference_works.limits_and_rights: Official store description only; no DFHack or game source was reviewed, and the separate DFHack project is not evidence about Dwarf Fortress internals. No playthrough or gameplay verification. Commercial work; no copying of prose, assets, code, names, or generated content.

reference_works.title: Wildermyth
observed_facts: The Modding Guide says most game data is JSON, user mods mirror the core game's directory layout, and the in-game Content and Comics Editor exposes events, abilities, aspects, campaigns, items, and monsters.

Story Inputs and Outputs documents checks over campaign/company state, legacy unlocks, present heroes, and other heroes; story roles can be chosen using traits, relationships, hooks, aspects, or stats.

The same guide enumerates supported outcomes including gear, body modifications, history lines, stat changes, hooks/aspects, map changes, relationships, unlocks, recruitment, and combat effects. It recommends clear risk/tradeoffs, permanent visible change for major moments, and mechanically simple supported outcomes.
The Legacy page describes a saved history of accomplishments and heroes, with recruitment in later campaigns preserving selected abilities subject to legacy tier.
reference_works.inference_and_yair_connection: The strongest lesson is an authoring contract: declare which campaign and character facts a story may inspect, select relevant roles, then connect a legible choice to a bounded set of supported effects and durable history. YAIR already has source-authored registries, situations, response predicates, validated effects, actors, relationships, attributed knowledge, and saved causes. The missing convenience is an editorial authoring workflow and reusable role/query layer, not another effects engine or a global hero legacy.
reference_works.limits_and_rights: Wiki authoring documentation and product design only, not Wildermyth code or complete player experience. No content, JSON files, icons, story text, characters, or assets are proposed for copying. Modding instructions themselves warn authors to contact an existing mod author before adapting and republishing their work.

reference_works.title: GURPS Infinite Worlds
observed_facts: The publisher describes a setting about parallel-world travel, with campaign roles including accidental travelers or Infinity Patrol agents.
The listing says its guidance covers designing and playing cross-setting characters and building alternate worlds from setting, story, and rules perspectives.
reference_works.inference_and_yair_connection: Useful tabletop comparator for making each destination's rules, entry premise, and traveler role explicit. Current YAIR owners include world identity, world instances, realm connections, boundary rules, and traveler profiles; it does not provide software evidence or justify adding a multiverse to the first milestone.
reference_works.limits_and_rights: This is a commercial tabletop book, not a software repository. Only the publisher's listing was used; the book was not acquired or accessed. Do not copy its setting text, names, trade dress, rules prose, or illustrations. The comparison is about the general authoring problem of distinct worlds and entry premises.

reference_works.title: Cavernous II

source_routes.kind: creator's published game and deployed script links
public source directory in the creator-profile GitHub Pages repository

observed_facts: The published interface documents per-clone action queues, synchronization and no-sync commands, repeat actions, zone routes, route estimates, and import/export for queues and saves.

The creator's GitHub profile identifies Sam Benner and links the public GitHub Pages repository. The live page loads named JavaScript modules; the repository additionally exposes the TypeScript source directory. Read-only source inspection confirmed concrete queue/action, clone, route, and zone modules. No scripts were executed.

The repository's LICENSE.md is a custom four-condition BSD-style license. It requires notices and disclaimer retention and says commercial use must first be authorized by Sam Benner or follow a good-faith attempt to obtain permission.
reference_works.inference_and_yair_connection: The useful design contrast is visible planned work across coordinated agents and routes. YAIR has jobs, common game clocks, clock leases, simulation commitments, and multi-world boundaries; it does not have clone-level synchronized queues or Cavernous route search. One readable authored preparation plan may be worth comparing, while reproducing queue management would add substantial interface and timing complexity.
reference_works.limits_and_rights: Interface evidence is published-page inspection plus the previously qualified entry in docs/NICHE_GAME_REFERENCES.md, not a game playthrough. Source coverage is limited to locating the project and inspecting selected TypeScript files; there was no repo-wide audit, build, execution, install, or gameplay test. Any direct code use needs an explicit license review and the listed commercial-use condition; page-hosted assets and other content were not separately licensed or audited.
